quotes.text: Now, Excel still has a job. You can use Excel to explore numbers, build a quick model, or answer a one-off question. But Excel usually holds a copy of the numbers.
quotes.why: Draws a clear line between spreadsheet analysis and the official finance record.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: If a correction is needed later, finance handles it through a controlled process. They don't quietly change history.
quotes.why: Captures the control principle behind closed accounting periods.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: The budget records what the company intended to do. The forecast shows what the company now expects to happen. Those are different questions.
quotes.why: Concise distinction between budget and forecast.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: A company can show a profit, but still wait for customers to pay. At the same time, suppliers and employees may need payment now. Profit tells part of the story. Cash tells you whether the company can meet its next commitments.
quotes.why: Explains why profit and cash flow must be read together.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: A team might discuss an invoice or share a document in Teams, but the official finance records stay safe inside Dynamics 365 finance.
quotes.why: Clarifies the role split between collaboration tools and the system of record.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: Dynamics 365 Finance keeps the official financial record in one place, linking purchase requests, purchase orders, receipts, supplier invoices and payments so nobody retypes data between tools.

The general ledger, chart of accounts and financial dimensions give every transaction a category and extra context such as department, location or project, so totals can be traced back to their source.
Budgets, forecasts and cash views answer different questions, and controls such as separated approvals, closed periods and a full audit trail protect the records behind every decision.
hook: Finance teams lose time when budgets, invoices and bank data live in different spreadsheets and systems. This Knowledge Nugget explains Dynamics 365 Finance in plain English for business users, managers and newcomers to ERP, from the first purchase request to the general ledger, budgeting, reporting and controls.
